revise verb

go over and correct

also revision, revised, rewrite, go over again, rework, revised edition, review, let’s review

classical

Suet. Aug. 34: lēgēs retractāvit (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 8.21.6 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. revise, rewrite
Traupman 31
Traupman 34

retractō, retractāre, retractāvī, retractātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

go over again, revise

Literally “take in hand again”; of mental work, to reconsider, go back over, revise a text or a law. It also means to withdraw, to refuse (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • recognōscō, recognōscere, recognōvī, recognitum — look over, review, check through

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.37 (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 83.2: diem meum recognōscam; M-O s.v. revise, rewrite

    Its first sense is to recognise (see recognize); it is also to look over and check: troops, accounts, a text. The editors’ word for revising a book (Morgan–Owens).

  • ēmendō, ēmendāre, ēmendāvī, ēmendātum — correct, emend (a text)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.16.4 (Lewis & Short); Quint. 2.2.7 (Lewis & Short)

    To free from faults; especially frequent of correcting what one has written (see reform).

  • incūdī reddere — rework, put back on the anvil

    phrase · also used · classical · Hor. A.P. 441: male tornātōs incūdī reddere versūs (M-O s.v. revise)

    Horace’s image for reworking badly turned lines; incūs is an anvil.

  • retractātiō, retractātiōnis f. — a going over again, revision; review

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Lewis & Short: “a retouching, revision”, chiefly in Augustine’s title Retractātiōnēs; Traupman 31

Examples

  • observābō mē prōtinus et, quod est ūtilissimum, diem meum recognōscam

    I will watch myself from now on and, what is most useful, go back over my daySen. Ep. 83.2

  • Hanc epistulam retractā antequam mittis.

    Go over this letter again before you send it.composed

  • Prōnōmina retractēmus.

    Let’s review the pronouns.Traupman 34

See also correct, reform, recognize.

SourcesLewis & Short: retracto · Lewis & Short: recognosco · Lewis & Short: emendo · Lewis & Short: incus

Lewis & Short: retractatio

Seneca from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-seneca-epistulae); the other passages as Lewis & Short or Morgan–Owens quotes them.

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. revise, rewrite.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
